name: Finance
description: Bank accounts, transactions, and budgets via Plaid.

screens.label: Budget
screens.description: This month's budget: money ready to assign, and each category's assigned, spent and available amounts.

screens.label: Transactions
screens.description: Every bank transaction grouped by day, with a search box, an All and Needs a look filter with a count, a Predicted badge on Moss's guesses, a category picker, an Always for this merchant switch that starts off, Confirm all, a category picker on every confirmed row to change its category, and a Show more button when a month has more than 200 rows.

screens.label: Accounts
screens.description: Connected banks listed by their real names (filled in on the next sync), balances, sync status, reconnect, and net worth.

screens.label: Getting started
screens.description: Connect a first bank, let Moss sort the spending, then build the budget together. With no bank keys set, an admin sees an Add bank keys button and everyone else sees Waiting on your admin. After the first sync it shows Your first budget, a draft built from up to three months of history, with a Build my budget with Moss button and a Start this budget button.

screens.label: Finance settings
screens.description: Everything Finance can configure: How much Moss does alone (Ask about everything, Handle routine and ask about new, Run it all and review weekly, or Custom; a new install starts on Handle routine and ask about new), the Moss can move up to dollar limit, a Customize list of per-action switches, Bank connection keys for admins, and this week's activity with an Undo button on each row and an Earlier weeks button. Freedom and dollar-limit controls stay unavailable until their reads succeed. Read failures have separate explanations and Retry; unverified fallback values are not presented as confirmed settings.

features.description: On Transactions, a Needs a look row has a category picker, a Confirm button and an Always for this merchant switch (off by default; on, the new category becomes a rule for that merchant). Confirm all N confirms every Needs a look row the filter and search show, keeps Moss's guessed categories, makes no rules, and disappears when none are left.

On Budget, type a dollar amount into a category's Assigned box and press Enter or click away to save it. Saving never asks for approval, and Available updates. If the save fails the box goes back to its old amount with an error. Every change is logged with who made it, and the log keeps only ids and amounts.

Getting started shows three steps (connect a bank, Moss sorts spending, build a budget together) with each step's state. A bank cannot be connected until an admin sets the bank keys in Finance settings.

After a bank has synced, Getting started builds a first budget from up to three months of history without asking Moss: each category's monthly average rounded up to the next five dollars, the middle monthly income, and merchants that charge about the same every month under Bills. It shows the plan total and how much income is still unplanned. Start this budget on that screen creates any missing categories and sets this month's amounts, then opens Budget. Only the button starts a budget; Moss in chat cannot. You can type a plan amount on any line, and Moss in chat can change, add or drop lines; the plan total and the unplanned amount always add up from the lines.

Moss sorts each new transaction into a category and marks the ones it is unsure about as Needs a look. Whether Moss confirms its own guesses for merchants you have confirmed before, and for new merchants, follows the Sort purchases settings. A guessed category still counts toward the budget while it waits for review.

In chat, Moss can move money between categories, set a category's assigned total, make a merchant rule, and add, rename or archive categories. Each reports what it changed, before and after, and is logged. A move or change larger than the Moss can move up to setting in Finance settings (default $100) asks for approval first; smaller ones follow the freedom setting.

On Finance settings, How much Moss does alone offers three steps plus Custom. Ask about everything makes Moss suggest every change. Handle routine, ask about new lets Moss sort merchants it knows and move money up to the limit, and asks about anything new. Run it all, review weekly lets Moss do everything up to the limit. Custom shows when the switches under Customize match none of the three. A step saves at once; if saving fails the choice goes back with an error. Until policy and limit reads succeed, controls are unavailable. Retry reloads failed settings without writing; a failed refresh keeps the last confirmed values.

On Finance settings, Moss can move up to, per move sets the dollar limit (a whole number from 0 to 100000, default 100). Moss asks for approval before any move or assigned total above it, at every step. It saves when you press Enter or click away; a bad or failed entry goes back to the saved amount with an error. Until policy and limit reads succeed, controls are unavailable. Retry reloads failed settings without writing; a failed refresh keeps the last confirmed values.

On Finance settings, Customize lists one switch per action Moss can take (sort purchases from merchants you have seen, move money between categories, sort purchases from new merchants, make merchant rules, add, rename or archive categories). On lets Moss do it alone, off makes Moss ask first. Connect a bank and Share an account show Always asks and cannot be switched.

On Finance settings, an admin sees Bank connection with the Plaid client ID and Plaid secret, each marked Saved or Not set, and a Replace button that takes a new value. Everyone else does not see this section. Saved values are never shown.

On Finance settings, the activity list shows this week's changes by you and by Moss, newest first, each with who did it and when. Undo reverses a row (a budget amount, a move between categories, a sorted purchase, a merchant rule, or a category added or archived) and says so inline if the data changed since. Earlier weeks loads the week before. With nothing yet it says Nothing yet.

assistantOnboarding.guidance: Finance holds the user's budget. Read before you write: call finance.budget.status or finance.transactions.query first. Amounts are integer cents. To move money, call finance.budget.move with both category ids; use "ready_to_assign" as the source when the money is unassigned. To set a category's total, call finance.budget.assign with previousCents, the total it has now. Example: "move 50 to groceries" with 80 ready to assign becomes finance.budget.move { fromCategoryId: "ready_to_assign", toCategoryId: "groceries", amountCents: 5000 }. Moves above the user's dollar limit ask for approval first. Report the before and after the tool returns. Never guess a category id; list categories first. While a first-budget draft is open, change it with finance.budget.draft.update after reading finance.budget.draft.get, and quote the totals it returns. Never start the budget; the user does that.

preferences.label: Moss can move up to
preferences.description: Moves above this amount ask first, at every freedom step.

assistantTools.name: finance.accounts.list
assistantTools.description: List connected bank accounts with live balances.

assistantTools.name: finance.setup.status
assistantTools.description: Report whether bank keys are set up and whether a bank is connected.

assistantTools.name: finance.connect.start
assistantTools.description: Start connecting a bank via Plaid Hosted Link; returns a link URL to open.

assistantTools.name: finance.connect.poll
assistantTools.description: Check pending bank connections and finish token exchange.

assistantTools.name: finance.sync.run-now
assistantTools.description: Sync accounts and transactions from Plaid now.

assistantTools.name: finance.transactions.query
assistantTools.description: Query synced transactions by month, account, category, or text.

assistantTools.name: finance.transaction.categorize
assistantTools.description: Set the category of a transaction from a merchant that already has confirmed history. Refuses a new merchant; use finance.transaction.categorize-new for that.

assistantTools.name: finance.transaction.categorize-new
assistantTools.description: Set the category of a transaction from a merchant with no confirmed history yet. Refuses a merchant that has it; use finance.transaction.categorize for that.

assistantTools.name: finance.budget.status
assistantTools.description: Show the envelope budget for a month: to-be-budgeted, assigned, activity, and available per category.

assistantTools.name: finance.budget.draft.get
assistantTools.description: Read the first-budget draft: its lines by group, the plan total, monthly income and the amount still unplanned. Reads only; the draft is started from the Getting started screen.

assistantTools.name: finance.budget.draft.update
assistantTools.description: Change one line of the first-budget draft: set its plan amount, rename it, move it to another group, or drop it. Read the draft first with finance.budget.draft.get for the draft id and category keys. To add a line that is not in the draft, give a new lowercase categoryKey with categoryName, groupName (Bills, Everyday, Fun or Savings) and amountCents. Returns the line and the draft total before and after; quote those numbers instead of adding them up. It cannot start the budget.

categoryKey.description: The line's category key from the draft, or a new lowercase slug to add a line.

amountCents.description: The monthly plan amount in integer cents (600 dollars is 60000).

dropped.description: True takes the line out of the budget.

assistantTools.name: finance.budget.assign
assistantTools.description: Set a category's assigned total for a month. Pass the total it has now as previousCents (read it from finance.budget.status); a wrong value is rejected. Returns the before and after totals.

categoryId.description: Id of an existing category. Never guess one; list categories first.

amountCents.description: The new assigned total in integer cents (50 dollars is 5000).

previousCents.description: The category's assigned total right now, in integer cents.

assistantTools.name: finance.budget.move
assistantTools.description: Move money between two categories for a month. Use fromCategoryId ready_to_assign to take unassigned money. Returns the before and after assigned totals.

fromCategoryId.description: Category to take from, or ready_to_assign for unassigned money.

toCategoryId.description: Category to give to. Must be a real category id.

amountCents.description: Amount to move, positive integer cents (50 dollars is 5000).

assistantTools.name: finance.rule.set
assistantTools.description: Always put one merchant in one category from now on. Replaces an earlier rule for that merchant and returns the before and after category.

merchant.description: The merchant name as it appears on transactions.

assistantTools.name: finance.category.upsert
assistantTools.description: Add a category (leave id out) or rename or regroup one (pass its id). Returns the before and after name and group.

id.description: Id of the category to change. Omit to add one.

groupName.description: The budget group the category sits in.

assistantTools.name: finance.category.archive
assistantTools.description: Archive a category. Refused while this month still has money assigned to it; move that money first.

id.description: Id of the category to archive.

assistantTools.name: finance.account.set-shared
assistantTools.description: Share or unshare one of your bank accounts with the household.

assistantTools.name: finance.reports.spending
assistantTools.description: Monthly spending by category and payee plus cash flow (income, outflow, net) over a window of recent months, including household-shared accounts.

assistantTools.name: finance.reports.net-worth
assistantTools.description: Daily net-worth series and current headline from your own account balance snapshots (liabilities negated).

assistantTools.name: finance.activity.list
assistantTools.description: List the changes Finance recorded between two times, newest first: who made each one (you or Moss), what it was in plain words, and whether it can be undone. Reads only.

from.description: Start of the window, an ISO timestamp.

to.description: End of the window, an ISO timestamp.
